bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for vertical integration and renewable energy; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; net debt equity at 0.11x provides flexibility; excess cash deployed in bonds and AIF for other income
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Pricing pressure from global tariffs and domestic competition; execution delay in dyeing unit commissioning; skill shortages during festive seasons; reliance on top 10 dealers for 99% revenue; no PLI benefits; margin expansion dependent on successful integration
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and structured; focused on execution of integration roadmap; transparent on margin compression being temporary; emphasizes working capital discipline and zero debt as competitive advantages; avoids overpromising on volume growth
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Teesta Spintex’s ₹3.37cr profit in H1 is largely from job work (30% of sales), not internal fabric conversion — meaning integration benefits are not yet fully captured in consolidated margins; the 82-inch loom advantage is a hidden differentiator in a market dominated by 210cm looms; AIF investment in equity markets adds non-operational income volatility
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Established presence in the denim fabric manufacturing sector with commercial production since 2016
- Integrated manufacturing infrastructure using Japanese Tsudakoma air-jet weaving technology, dobby and cam-motion systems and multi-colour weft insertion capability
- Diverse denim product portfolio spanning multiple constructions, shades, weights and finishes, serving varied customer requirements
- In-house renewable energy assets (2 MW windmill and 852 kW rooftop solar) meeting approximately 90% of the facility's energy requirement, lowering energy cost exposure and carbon footprint per metre of fabric
- Forward integration across the textile value chain via the 100% wholly owned subsidiary Teesta Spintex Private Limited
- Strong industry experience and established relationships across the textile value chain
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cotton and raw material price volatility — Denim weaving is raw-material intensive and management lists volatility in cotton and other raw material prices first among both threats and business risks; the Company has no disclosed hedging or pass-through mechanism, so input swings feed directly into gross margin.
- Margin compression from weak sales realisations — Standalone revenue fell 3.82% in FY 2025-26, which the Board attributes primarily to lower sales realisations and changing market dynamics; cost control lowered operating expenses but softer margins still impacted standalone profitability, showing realisation pressure passes through to earnings.
- Energy, labour and other operating cost inflation — Explicitly flagged as a threat. Denim weaving and processing is power-intensive; captive solar and wind cover roughly 90% of facility energy needs, which mitigates but does not eliminate exposure to grid tariff, labour and other operating cost movements.
- Intense competition from domestic and international textile manufacturers — Flagged as a threat in the SWOT and repeated in the risk-management discussion. Denim fabric is a fragmented, largely commoditised market where competitive intensity constrains pricing power.
- Shifting consumer preferences and fashion trends — Management flags changes in consumer preferences and fashion trends as a threat; denim demand is fashion-led, so a mix shift away from the Company's constructions, shades, weights or finishes can strand capacity and inventory.
- Macroeconomic, regulatory and supply-chain disruption — The Company cites macroeconomic conditions, regulatory changes and disruptions in domestic or global supply chains among its threats, and the cautionary statement repeats economic conditions, government policies, market conditions, industry developments, availability of raw materials and demand-supply dynamics as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.
- Single-product, single-site concentration — The Company is a single-activity denim fabric manufacturer operating from one manufacturing facility of approximately 46,757 square metres, with no change in the nature of business during the year; there is no product or site diversification to absorb a demand or operational shock at that facility.
- Related-party dependence and governance exemptions as an SME-platform issuer — Loans taken from and given to promoter-family members, HUFs and group entities (Sparsh Fabrics, Rikin Fabrics, Rikin Chemical, Bharat Polyfab) plus purchases and sales with those entities are a recurring feature of the year. Because the Company is listed on the SME Platform of BSE, Regulations 17 to 27 corporate-governance requirements and the BRSR are not mandatorily applicable, so external governance and sustainability oversight is lighter than for main-board peers.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Core: Denim weaving (89.9% utilization); Forward integration: Teesta Spintex finishing unit (₹3.37cr PAT in H1, 30% job work); Backward integration: New dyeing unit (₹55cr capex, commissioning Dec’26/Jan’27); Renewable: 65% power from renewables, targeting 90% by FY27 with ₹8-9cr capex

business.body: Incorporated in 2010 with commercial production commencing in 2016, the Company manufactures a diverse range of denim fabrics across varied constructions, shades, weights and finishes for customers across the fashion and apparel value chain. Manufacturing runs on modern air-jet weaving technology, including Japanese Tsudakoma air-jet machines, advanced dobby and cam-motion systems and multi-colour weft insertion capability. During FY 2025-26 the Company added forward integration into the textile value chain through the acquisition of Teesta Spintex Private Limited as a 100% wholly owned subsidiary.

latest_quarter.body: Current EBITDA margin 2.6% due to pricing compromise to maintain working capital; dyeing integration expected to add ₹12cr PAT; renewable energy to save ₹4.5-4.65cr annually (from ₹2.65cr today); cost advantage from 65% renewable power, zero debt, and wider looms (82-inch) lowers unit cost vs peers

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 7-8% YoY; EBITDA margin: Targeting 7-8% by FY28; Order inflow: No explicit guidance; Capex/Commissioning: ₹55cr for backward dyeing unit (Dec’26/Jan’27); ₹8-9cr for renewable energy (Q1FY27)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Potential diversification into non-denim technical fabrics if denim demand softens; no B2C or brand launch planned; capacity expansion contingent on integration ROI
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Broaden the business platform and strengthen the Company's position across the textile value chain, with forward integration through the 100% wholly owned subsidiary Teesta Spintex Private Limited as the key initiative of the year.
- Enhance product capabilities and improve value creation by developing a more integrated approach to the Company's textile activities.
- Prioritise operational excellence through efficient capacity utilisation, prudent procurement, effective working capital management and continuous process improvement.
- Maintain focus on product quality, process discipline and cost management to protect margins in a period of softer realisations.
- Continue integrating in-house solar and wind renewable energy to reduce dependence on conventional power and lower the carbon footprint per metre of fabric produced.
- Retain profits rather than distribute a dividend, conserving resources for future growth and expansion plans.
- Expand market presence and strengthen customer relationships across the denim and apparel value chain.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion action in FY 2025-26 was inorganic rather than greenfield: on 9 May 2025 it acquired 100% of the equity share capital of Teesta Spintex Private Limited, which thereby became a wholly owned subsidiary. Management describes the acquisition as a strategic step towards forward integration of the textile value chain, intended to strengthen the Group's presence across complementary stages of the textile business, create operational synergies and support a more integrated business platform. No new denim weaving line, capacity addition, commissioning date or ramp-up timeline is disclosed for the existing facility, which continues to operate at an installed capacity of approximately 19.2 million metres per annum across a manufacturing area of approximately 46,757 square metres. On renewable energy the Company states that substantial investments in solar and wind infrastructure were made during FY 2022-23 and that no significant additional capital investment was made specifically towards energy conservation equipment during the year ended 31 March 2026; the existing 2 MW Amreli windmill and 852 kW rooftop solar plant continued to be operated rather than expanded. The Company also states it will continue to assess opportunities for enhancing product capabilities and pursuing appropriate growth opportunities, but attaches no project, quantum or date to that intent. NOTE: the '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE - CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' block supplied with this bundle arrived caption-only - the captions from pages 127 and 155 ('The estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for' / 'against which advance have been paid') are present but the corresponding amounts were truncated, so no rupee capital-commitment quantum is recoverable.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing domestic demand for denim and casual apparel is the principal stated demand driver.
- Expansion of organised retail, branded apparel and e-commerce channels widens the addressable market.
- Increasing demand for value-added, stretch, premium and sustainable denim fabrics supports a richer product mix.
- Forward integration through the wholly owned subsidiary is expected to open synergies across the textile value chain and support enhanced value creation.
- Government initiatives supporting domestic textile manufacturing and value-chain development are cited as an opportunity.
- FY 2025-26 standalone revenue declined 3.82% year on year, which management attributes primarily to lower sales realisations and changing market dynamics; effective cost control lowered operating expenses but softer margins still impacted standalone profitability.
- Management is cautiously optimistic about the long-term prospects of the denim and textile sector while acknowledging cotton and energy cost volatility and intense domestic and international competition.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Shanti Spintex delivered record H1FY26 revenue of ₹382cr driven by capacity utilization of 89.9% and Teesta Spintex acquisition, but PAT declined due to pricing pressure; the path to margin expansion now hinges on backward integration into dyeing (commissioning Dec’26/Jan’27) and renewable energy capex, which together are expected to lift PAT to ₹30cr by FY28.

open.item: Prescribed CSR expenditure of Rs 30.41 lakhs, being 2% of the average net profit of Rs 1,520.46 lakhs for the last three financial years, applies for the year under review.
The Company will continue to develop synergies across the textile value chain from the forward integration represented by its wholly owned subsidiary Teesta Spintex Private Limited.
The Company remains focused on enhancing operational efficiencies, expanding market presence and strengthening customer relationships going forward.
